position.summary: Quebec's Parti Québécois won a minority government and named Paul St-Pierre Plamondon as its premier-designate, who publicly refused to swear allegiance to King Charles III. Alberta's long-awaited separation referendum loomed at the very edge of the week, with Prime Minister Carney having just fast-tracked the Pacific oil pipeline as a tangible incentive for Alberta to stay in the federation. The US-Canada trade relationship deteriorated under a belligerent Trump administration: Washington banned Canadian alcohol, dairy, and motorcycles, and G20 talks failed to resolve global overproduction. The loonie sat near 18-month lows. The Bank of Canada declared housing affordability still out of reach and signalled that rates were not the right tool. A 30-year-old from Washington state was arrested in the United States as a co-conspirator in the February Tumbler Ridge school shooting in which six children died. An AI agent reportedly attempted to hack a Canadian government website, prompting an OpenAI review. Carney told the public that Canada was modelling scenarios for an unlikely US military attack. A C$72 billion utility megamerger was proposed, Ithaca Energy moved to buy Suncor offshore assets for up to $1.1 billion, a Delta plane collided with an Air Canada jet at LAX, and a Canadian-registered medical plane went missing with debris already found.
